espn-603999.headline: France ask a scrum-half to fix a 2005 problem
beats: South African press spent the build-up reminding Paris that France have not beaten South Africa at the Stade de France since 2005. France's answer is Antoine Dupont at fly-half, moved there by an injury crisis at 10.

Injuries have reshaped the rest of the side too. Only three of the starters from last November's 17–32 home defeat start again. France have lost twice this year, once 32–34 in New Zealand, and put 54 on Fiji last weekend while South Africa were putting 66 on Italy.
Rassie Erasmus has made late changes again, sending his named front row, Malcolm Marx among them, to the bench. Win, and France go up to third while South Africa hand first place to New Zealand.
Both lead their conferences, which is the grand-final pairing at Twickenham. It makes this a rehearsal, with both sides still changing the cast.

espn-604000.headline: Contepomi would take a win by half a point to nil
beats: Felipe Contepomi is under fierce criticism in the Argentine press. His side have one win this year, against Wales, and were beaten 42–12 by Ireland on 6 November. Give him a win by half a point to nil, he says, and he will correct the rest the following week.
Italy look like the side to provide it. They have lost five straight, conceded 66 to South Africa on 7 November and have 16 players injured. They have not beaten Argentina since 2008.

Pablo Matera captains in place of the injured Montoya, and Argentina carry a 6+2 bench. Matera called it "un pack pesante" and called Italy strong at the set piece, which is where the game will be decided. If Italy win it there, they rise to 9th, above Fiji and Wales.
A week later Argentina go to France, and Italy host Fiji, the only other side without a point. Half a point to nil would do for either coach.

espn-604001.headline: Wales have been trying since 1953
beats: New Zealand have won 34 in a row against Wales since the last Welsh win, in 1953. The most recent came on this ground last November, 26–52.

Wales beat Japan 28–21 last time out, but six of their lineout throws went astray. Before that they were held scoreless in South Africa, 0–43. New Zealand have scored seven tries in each of their last three games, against Scotland and against Australia twice.

Beauden Barrett captains New Zealand for the first time. It is his 149th Test, which takes him past Richie McCaw on the country's appearance list. Dave Rennie has marked Jac Morgan at the breakdown, and wants to deal with him "before he can cause us stress".
A Welsh win would move them up to 9th, above Fiji. That is a modest reward for ending 73 years.

espn-604002.headline: Eddie Jones knows where England keep the spare key
beats: Jones coached England from 2015 to 2022, longer than anyone has. He brings Japan to Allianz Stadium having spent the build-up telling his old side they do not like "unorthodox" rugby.

Steve Borthwick has answered with 10 personnel changes, keeping just three players in the same positions from the 45–22 win over Australia. Maro Itoje's counter-plan fits in one word, said three times: "We need to be alive, alive, alive."

England have never lost to Japan and have put a half-century on them in each of the last two meetings. Japan lost 21–28 in Cardiff on 7 November, and only a Japan win by 16 or more would push England down to sixth in the world, below Scotland.
New Zealand are at home to England on 21 November. Jones would like England's inexperienced side to spend this week thinking about him instead.

espn-604003.headline: Ireland get their South Africans a week early
beats: Jake White took over Fiji last month and brought in Gert Smal, a fellow South African who coached Ireland's forwards to the 2009 Grand Slam. The actual Springboks come to the Aviva Stadium on 21 November.
Andy Farrell has made seven changes, with Tadhg Beirne captain. White's selection was shaped by injuries, and he is banking on Josua Tuisova to make his mark.

Ireland scored six tries in a 42–12 win over Argentina on 6 November. Fiji conceded 54 in Paris the next day. A Fiji win would drop Ireland to fifth in the world, below France and England, which is an awkward way to greet the Springboks.
Dublin is looking past it as well. Just over 46,000 tickets have gone for a 51,700 ground, even after the IRFU cut adult prices during the week.

espn-604004.headline: Two 21–43 defeats, one game to stop the leak
beats: Scotland lost to New Zealand by that score at Murrayfield on 7 November. Australia lost to them by the same score at home in October. Since then England have put a record 45 on Australia, the third game running in which they conceded over 40, while Scotland have let in 38 or more in five of their last six Tests.

Les Kiss starts Carter Gordon at fly-half, his first game since breaking his leg in the 28–28 draw with Argentina in Mendoza in September. Rob Valetini is back on the blindside for the breakdown, and Joseph Suaalii moves to outside centre after four Tests on the wing.
An Australia win by any margin lifts them above Scotland into sixth in the world. That would be a generous return for a side with one win in four in this competition.

Scotland bring back Darcy Graham, their all-time leading try scorer, and Blair Kinghorn at full-back. Ewan Ashman stays at hooker. He scored a hat-trick against New Zealand and still finished 22 points behind.

espn-604005.headline: New Zealand lost here by 14. Now they need 16
beats: England won 33–19 when these two last met, at home on 15 November 2025. Turn that margin round, add two points, and New Zealand go past South Africa to first in the world.

Both sides arrive scoring freely. New Zealand have run in seven tries in each of their last three, against Australia twice and Scotland. England put seven on Australia on 8 November. Both also know what South Africa can do to them: England lost 45–21 in July, New Zealand 43–28 in September.
England have Japan first. Eddie Jones, Japan's coach and once England's, made England favourites for that one. He also suggested their minds might already be on New Zealand.
He meant it as a weakness. On the evidence of last November, it could just as easily be the plan.

espn-604006.headline: Scotland lost 21–43 twice. Townsend blames the 22
beats: New Zealand scored seven tries at Murrayfield on 7 November and won 43–21, the same score Ireland put on Scotland in March. Townsend's diagnosis was not the tackling but the offside and the slow rolling away that let them into the 22, which he called "individual responsibility".

His other line was arithmetic: "if you are giving those entries to the best teams in the world, they are looking to score over 50% of the time." Japan are 12th, not the best, but they put 63 on USA and 57 on Canada in September, and lost only 21–28 in Wales last time out.
Darcy Graham, 29, is back from a bicep tear with 38 tries in 57 Tests. He was meant to miss the autumn. Scotland need someone scoring at the other end.
Lose, and Scotland drop below Australia in the world rankings, a week after hosting them at Murrayfield. Their next chance to put it right is Italy in February.

espn-604007.headline: Five cards last time. Ireland would settle for none.
beats: Their last meeting, on 22 November 2025, was also at the Aviva. South Africa won 24–13, the Irish scrum was dominated, and James Ryan's card was a 20-minute red.
Andrew Porter has not played for Ireland since that November and has spent the year stewing over the scrum. His plan is to "Swing at it".

South Africa are unbeaten in the Nations Championship and put 66 past Italy last time out. Ireland's one defeat was 21–40 in New Zealand, and they beat Argentina 42–12 at home on 6 November. Win here and Ireland drop South Africa to second in the world, behind New Zealand.
A week out, Ryan said Ireland were "not thinking about South Africa". Porter, it seems, has thought about little else.

espn-604008.headline: Bottom of the table, playing for ninth in the world
beats: Italy are last of twelve in the Nations Championship and Fiji are eleventh, with eight defeats between them. Fiji are also ninth in the world, and an Italy win in Udine takes that place from them, putting Italy above Fiji and Wales.

Italy have lost five straight and conceded 66 to South Africa on 7 November. Captain Giacomo Nicotera called the review of that game hard, with too many penalties. Fiji let in 54 against France the same day, a fortnight after beating Japan 34–28.
Both have a game first. Italy host Argentina in Genoa, and Jake White has Fiji set up in Dublin for Ireland.
Stay bottom of their conferences and finals weekend pairs them again, for eleventh. Ninth in the world is the better thing to carry out of November.

espn-604009.headline: Argentina bring a Top 14 squad and one win to Paris
beats: Felipe Contepomi's squad is made up mostly of Top 14 players, so Saint-Denis is close to their day job. Their only win this year came against Wales, and not easily. Rugbyrama counts them among the Nations Championship's great disappointments, a year out from the World Cup in Australia.
They lost to South Africa, Australia and England by seven points or fewer, then conceded 42 in Dublin. France have scored 54, 42 and 42 in their last three.
Both have a game first. France host South Africa, with Antoine Dupont moved to fly-half for an injury crisis at 10. Argentina go to Italy needing a response.
An Argentina win would lift them above Australia in the world rankings and drop France below England. That is a lot to ask of a side whose last trip north cost them 42 points.

espn-604010.headline: Australia have leaked 40-plus in three straight Tests
beats: New Zealand put 50 and 43 on them in October. England added 45 on 8 November. Before that run, Australia beat South Africa 42–38, so the scoring end is not where the trouble lies.

Wales are hardly a wall either. They beat Japan 28–21 on 7 November, a win Planet Rugby reckons they were lucky to hold, and they host New Zealand before this. Australia go to Murrayfield first, with Carter Gordon back at fly-half after fracturing his leg in the draw with Argentina in Mendoza in September.
Win in Cardiff and Wales go up to 9th, with Australia dropping to 8th, below the same Argentina they sit one point above in their conference.
It is the last Test of the year for both. Wales go to France in February. Australia next play Hong Kong at a World Cup in October 2027, which is a long time to sit with the tape.
